newsitem.title: CHINA: China's personal income tax revenue up for 1996.
newsitem.headline: China's personal income tax revenue up for 1996.

text.p: China's personal income tax revenue soared by 46.9 percent to 19.3 billion yuan ($2.3 billion) in 1996, but many people were still evading taxes, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
The biggest single source of individual income tax revenue was Beijing, which accounted for about 2.27 billion yuan of the total, it said quoting statistics from the State Administration of Taxation.

Shanghai was in second place with 2.16 billion yuan, while southern Guangdong province was third with 1.91 billion yuan and the eastern provinces of Jiangsu and Fujian followed, collecting 974 million yuan and 890 million yuan respectively, it said.
Most of those taxed were private business people, but many people were still failing to pay their income taxes, an administration official said.
"A lack of the awareness to pay the income tax and an undesirable social taxation environment are the two major problems," he said.
In some regions, government departments even interfered in tax collection, he said but did not elaborate.
The difficulties of tax collection were exacerbated by insufficient checks on cash incomes and transactions, he said.
A greater effort should be made to collect taxes from people in the high-income bracket, such as entertainers, and people in the advertising industry, the official said.

China introduced its first individual income tax law in 1980 and a 1994 revision outlines graduated tax rates of five percent to 45 percent, with the minimum taxable income set at 800 yuan a month and incomes of more than 100,000 yuan a month falling into the highest tax bracket.
